tip: On foot = με τα πόδια, literally 'with the feet': πήγαινα με τα πόδια (píyena me ta pódhia).
Two imperfects = two actions running together: τραγουδούσε όταν μαγείρευε (traghudhúse ótan mayíreve).
Μικρός on its own can stand for 'as a kid': μικρός δεν έτρωγα (mikrós dhen étrogha = as a kid I didn't eat).
Από τα οχτώ μου = from age eight, literally 'from my eight' (apó ta okhtó mu).
Wishes normally sit in the imperfect: ήθελα να γίνω (íthela na yíno = I wanted to become).
Στης γιαγιάς (stis yayás) = at grandma's – the word for the house is left unsaid, like English 'at grandma's'.
Ξέρω (kséro = I know) has no separate one-off past: ήξερα (íksera = I knew) covers it, since knowing is usually a state rather than a single event.
Από μικρή (apó mikrí) = ever since I was little, said by a woman – a man says από μικρός (apó mikrós).
Παλιά + imperfect = used to: παλιά δούλευα (paliá dhúleva = I used to work).
Πέφτω για ύπνο is literally 'I fall for sleep', the everyday 'go to bed': έπεφτα για ύπνο (épefta ya ípno).
Per day = τη μέρα: πέντε καφέδες τη μέρα (pénde kafédhes ti méra = five coffees a day).
English 'would' for habits = plain imperfect: κοιτούσα για ώρες (kitúsa ya óres).
Μαζί της = with her: γελούσαμε μαζί της (yelúsame mazí tis); with him is μαζί του (mazí tu).
Birthdays are plural in Greek: τα γενέθλια (ta yenéthlia = the birthday).
No 'about' needed after σκέφτομαι: σκεφτόμουν τις διακοπές (skeftómun tis dhiakopés = I was thinking the holidays) – the noun follows directly.
Κάθε φορά που = every time that: κάθε φορά που ερχόταν (káthe forá pu erkhótan).
Notes are 'held' in Greek: κρατούσα σημειώσεις (kratúsa simiósis = I took notes).
Μόνος μου = on my own, and a woman says μόνη μου (móni mu): μάθαινα μόνος μου (máthena mónos mu).
Νόμιζα (nómiza) = I thought – usually a belief that turned out wrong: νόμιζα ότι ήξερες (nómiza óti íkseres = I thought you knew).
Ongoing effort = imperfect: έψαχνα για έξι μήνες (épsakhna ya éksi mínes = I was searching for six months).
Σπούδαζα (spúdhaza) means being enrolled – studying for a degree. Tonight's homework is a different verb, διαβάζω (dhiavázo).
'Prefer X to Y' uses από (apó = from): προτιμούσα το βουνό από τη θάλασσα (protimúsa to vunó apó ti thálasa) – 'from' where English says 'to'.
Έχει κόσμο = it's busy, literally 'it has people': είχε κόσμο (íkhe kósmo = it was busy).
Greek says 'we were friends with Yiannis': ήμασταν φίλοι με τον Γιάννη (ímastan fíli me ton Yáni).
'It's sunny' uses έχω (ékho = have): είχε ήλιο (íkhe ílio = there was sun / it was sunny).
Shops really did shut at midday: τα μαγαζιά έκλειναν (ta maghaziá éklinan = the shops used to close) for the afternoon rest – many small shops still do.
Rooms 'see' in Greek: το δωμάτιό μου έβλεπε στη θάλασσα (to dhomátió mu évlepe sti thálasa = my room looked out on the sea).
Φοβάμαι (fováme) takes the thing directly, with no 'of': φοβόταν τη βροχή (fovótan ti vrokhí = was afraid of the rain).
With δεν (dhen), κανέναν = anyone: δεν ήξερα κανέναν (dhen íksera kanénan = I knew no one).
Γίνεται (yínete) = takes place: γινόταν γιορτή (yinótan yortí = a celebration was held).
